title: Discovering Plastic-Binding Peptides with Favorable Affinity, Water Solubility, and Binding Specificity Through Deep Learning and Biophysical Modeling
authors: Tianhong Tan; Michael Bergman; Carol K Hall; Fengqi You
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习与生物物理建模设计塑料结合肽，虽涉及分子互作与MD模拟，但对象为肽-塑料而非蛋白质-DNA，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution, which is present in the ecosystem in vast quantities, adversely affects human health and the environment, making it imperative to develop methods for its mitigation. The challenge of detecting or capturing MPs could potentially be addressed using plastic-binding peptides (PBPs). The ideal PBP for MP remediation would not only bind strongly to plastic, but also have other properties such as high solubility in water or great binding specificity to a certain plastic. However, the scarcity or absence of known PBPs for common plastics along with the lack of methods that can discover PBPs with all of the desired properties precludes the development of peptide-based MP remediation strategies. In this study, we discovered short linear PBPs with high predicted water solubility and binding specificity by employing an in-silico discovery pipeline that combines deep learning and biophysical modeling. First, a long short-term memory (LSTM) network was trained on biophysical modeling data to predict peptide affinity to plastic. High affinity peptides were generated by pairing the trained LSTM with a Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) algorithm. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations showed that the PBPs discovered for polyethylene, the most common plastic, had 15% lower binding free energy than PBPs obtained using biophysical modeling alone. PBPs with both high affinity and high predicted solubility in water were found by including the CamSol solubility score in the MCTS peptide scoring function, increasing the average solubility score from 0.2 to 0.9, while only minimally decreasing affinity for polyethylene. The framework also discovered peptides with high binding specificity between polystyrene and polyethylene, two major constituents of MP pollution, using a competitive MCTS approach that optimized the difference in affinity between the two plastics. MD simulations showed that competitive MCTS increased the binding specificity of PBPs for polystyrene and identified peptides with relatively great preference for either of the two plastics. The framework can readily be applied to design PBPs for other types of plastic. Overall, the high-affinity PBPs with desirable properties discovered by marrying artificial intelligence and biophysics can be valuable for remediating MP pollution and protecting the health of humans and the environment.
abstract_zh: 微塑料（MP）污染在生态系统中大量存在，对人类健康和环境产生不利影响，因此亟需开发缓解措施。检测或捕获微塑料的挑战可能通过塑料结合肽（PBPs）得到解决。理想的用于微塑料修复的PBP不仅应强效结合塑料，还应具备其他特性，如高水溶性或对特定塑料的高结合特异性。然而，常见塑料的已知PBP稀缺或缺失，加之缺乏能发现具备所有期望特性的PBP的方法，阻碍了基于肽的微塑料修复策略的发展。在本研究中，我们通过结合深度学习与生物物理建模的计算机模拟发现流程，发现了具有高预测水溶性和结合特异性的短线性PBPs。首先，在生物物理建模数据上训练了一个长短期记忆（LSTM）网络，以预测肽对塑料的亲和力。通过将训练好的LSTM与蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）算法配对，生成了高亲和力肽。分子动力学（MD）模拟显示，针对最常见塑料——聚乙烯所发现的PBPs，其结合自由能比仅使用生物物理建模获得的PBPs低15%。通过在MCTS肽评分函数中纳入CamSol溶解度评分，找到了兼具高亲和力和高预测水溶性的PBPs，平均溶解度评分从0.2提升至0.9，而对聚乙烯的亲和力仅略有下降。该框架还通过竞争性MCTS方法，优化了两种塑料之间的亲和力差异，发现了在聚苯乙烯和聚乙烯（微塑料污染的两大主要成分）之间具有高结合特异性的肽。MD模拟表明，竞争性MCTS提高了PBPs对聚苯乙烯的结合特异性，并识别出对两种塑料中任一种具有相对较强偏好的肽。该框架可轻松应用于设计其他类型塑料的PBPs。总体而言，通过人工智能与生物物理学的结合所发现的高亲和力且具备理想特性的PBPs，对于缓解微塑料污染及保护人类健康和环境具有重要价值。
